articles.title_orig: WTA roundup: Diana Shnaider passes early test in China
articles.title_zh: WTA roundup: Diana Shnaider passes early test in China
articles.content_orig:
Sixth-seeded Russian Diana Shnaider survived a 7-5, 7-6 (4) challenge from Kazakhstan’s Yulia Putintseva in first-round action on Tuesday at the Ningbo Open in China.
Shnaider rallied from a 5-2 deficit in the opening set and dug out of a 5-3 hole in the second set to finish the match in 2 hours and 26 minutes. Shnaider overcame 49 unforced errors — 28 more than Putintseva — by saving nine of 14 break points and compiling a 34-18 advantage in winners.
No. 5 Belinda Bencic of Switzerland, the only other seeded player in action, was leading 6-3, 1-1 when Latvia’s Jelena Ostapenko was forced to retire after 62 minutes. Bencic’s second-round opponent at the WTA 500 event will be Poland’s Katarzyna Kawa, who rallied for a 1-6, 6-2, 6-4 defeat of Ukraine’s Daria Snigur.
Also moving to the second round were Russia’s Ekaterina Alexandrova, Italy’s Jasmine Paolini, Uzbekistan’s Polina Kudermetova and the Czech Republic’s Sara Bejlek.
No. 1 seed Ann Li avoided the upset bug in Osaka and rallied for a 5-7, 6-0, 6-3 first-round win against Australia’s Emerson Jones in just under 2 hours in Osaka.
The 26-year-old American delivered 10 aces, saved five of eight break points and posted a decisive 34-13 edge in winners. Li will face Turkey’s Zeynep Sonmez in the second round of the WTA 250 event after she also came from behind for a 3-6, 6-4, 6-3 defeat of Australia’s Maya Joint.
No. 2 Peyton Stearns and No. 7 Oleksandra Oliynykova made early exits. Stearns retired trailing 4-0 in the third set against Katerina Siniakova of the Czech Republic, while fellow American Mary Stoiana knocked out Ukraine’s Oliynykova 6-2, 6-3. No. 8 seed Katie Boulter of Great Britain was a 6-3, 6-1 winner against Japan’s Himeno Sakatsume.
Others advancing to the second round included Poland’s Magda Linette, Czech Tereza Valentova, Croatia’s Antonia Ruzic, Japan’s Moyuka Uchijima and Kayla Day. Day only needed 71 minutes to eliminate U.S. compatriot Sofia Kenin 6-3, 6-2.

articles.title_orig: Stock Market Today: Dow Jumps 500 Points on Mideast Hopes; Brent Crude Drops — Live Updates
articles.title_zh: Stock Market Today: Dow Jumps 500 Points on Mideast Hopes; Brent Crude Drops — Live Updates
articles.content_orig:
Get Mike Santoli's Market Memo in your inbox first. SUBSCRIBE HERE
In a previous life, when I routinely shut down New York City bars, the end of Daylight Saving Time was an annual bonus, as 2am on a Saturday night instantly became 1am, leaving three more hours until closing time.
The financial markets now are undergoing several forms of late-cycle unease, and Wall Street is now looking for earnings season and the passage of the midterm elections to turn back the clock before last call.
To be clear, this remains a bull market, the S&P 500 's uptrend unbroken, with constant rotations between AI tech and remainder of the market fitfully supporting the tape, with pullbacks limited to 3% for half a year.
Still, the index is now chopping around a flattish 50-day moving average at levels first reached 11 weeks ago, the AI-hardware cohort has badly broken stride, bank stocks are trading poorly off their results, and credit markets are getting colicky.
Late last week, the urgent selling in semiconductors and data-center equities and debt resembled the sort of forced-unwind rhythms from July, when a big upstart tech hedge fund was in the process of being all but liquidated.
A tentative bounce in semiconductor stocks Monday was minimally reassuring, in that it meant we didn't get the further disorderly purge many had braced for over the weekend (when S&P 500 "perpetual" futures on Hyperliquid had a sudden head-fake drop late Saturday).
Jason Hunter, technical strategist at JP Morgan, sets out the crucial question for a market sending mixed signals:
"With the bearish seasonal window now closing, we are left wondering if the market is in the terminal phase of a sequence of rolling corrections ahead of a typical late-year rally. Or are the plentiful amounts of bearish internal, momentum, and intra-market divergences that have formed as the S&P 500 index has decelerated below longer-term channel resistance setting the market up for a larger and more correlated setback?"
He leans toward a more cautious interpretation, keeping the S&P 500 on a short leash that extends about 2.5% lower to 7500, a break of which would lose the tape the benefit of the doubt.
Based on precedent and circumstance, the market "should" be setting up for a comeback that could reset the clock in bulls' favor. The fourth quarter after a midterm election year, historically, is overwhelmingly positive. Earnings growth projected to exceed a 20% year-over-year growth rate again this quarter can hardly be viewed as anything but a positive at least to bolster the fundamental case.
Still, against most probabilities, 2018 happened. By which I mean a 19% S&P 500 peak-to-trough decline in the fourth quarter of a midterm-election year, one that saw total S&P 500 earnings grow by more than 20%.
The 2018 tailspin had followed a massive momentum crescendo and reversal several months earlier, which gave way to an erratic tape that couldn't absorb what seemed at the time relatively unthreatening Federal Reserve tightening actions.
Financial conditions have now been tightening by means of higher Treasury yields, somewhat wider corporate-credit spreads, an uptick in volatility and a stronger U.S. dollar.
It's become common to hear investors insist that "the market is doing the Fed's tightening for it," suggesting Chairman Kevin Warsh himself should show restraint in further hiking rates despite the recent upturn in inflation. Sure, but the reason the markets are tightening is, in part, because Warsh himself expressed resolve in fighting inflation and investors therefore believe he'll take short-term rates up a bit more.
How Warsh treats these market shifts after next week's Fed meeting is another node of disagreement on the Street.
Bank of America economist Aditya Bhave says the markets are testing the Fed's pain threshold with the Nasdaq retreating 5% and credit spreads flaring a bit. The market has taken recent Fedspeak to suggest very low chances of an October rate hike, even though Warsh himself has decried forward guidance and said the Fed shouldn't suppress normal market volatility. Bhave is maintaining his non-consensus prediction for an October hike, conceding it's a close call.
Morgan Stanley equity strategist Mike Wilson takes the other side on the Fed's response to the recent tensing up of markets: "We think some acknowledgement of this tightening by Warsh would be well received by rate-sensitive areas that have already derated notably. Conversely, an indifference to this tightening may invoke memories of Powell's 2018 'auto-pilot' remarks in reference to that tightening episode."
The "de-rating" and "de-risking" process has surely been notable in recent weeks, with small and cyclical stocks under significant valuation pressure and hedge funds aggressively repositioning out of tech.
Is it enough to enliven buyers into or after the election?
Ned Davis Research thematic strategist Pat Tschosik notes his firm's proprietary market-breadth reading Big Mo Tape tentatively turning higher from oversold readings. "If Big Tech disappoints on Q3 earnings, we may get a full market washout and Big Mo could head even lower like it did in October 2023. Perhaps this is what is needed to set up for a post-midterm-election rally into yearend."
John Kolovos of Macro Risk Advisors sees a similar level to JPMorgan's as the market's breaking point, while evaluating his sentiment indicator.
Kolovos on the latest reading: "A noticeable sentiment reset is underway on the heels of the AI trade unwind and tightening financial conditions.  The good news is that bullish sentiment is finally starting to wash out, which should set the stage for a year-end rally. However, a break below the mid-September lows on the S&P 500 near 7,500 would warn that something more than a routine pullback is unfolding."
-There's something of a paradox at work – or a collective investor blind spot - when the bond market is finally offering relatively safe income after many years of meager yields and yet people continue to rush for the engineered income delivered by options-selling ETFs. This CNBC.com piece offers a thorough, smart rundown of these strategies, complete with warnings of tax pitfalls. This Bloomberg report details a more aggressive approach through funds many investors don't quite understand, while introducing me to the community of self-styled "dividend nomads."
-Anthropic's proposal to place 5% of its equity into a "public benefit fund" to help groups potentially disadvantaged by AI's propagation and Elon Musk's stated offer to give one of his SpaceX shares to every American child via Trump Accounts suggest that anxiety over AI economic disruption is going from simmer to boil.
We can cynically observe that such efforts also hype these companies' world-changing potency, a form of marketing through scare-mongering sheathed in generosity.  But the concern over AI's impact on current worker groups is well-placed, even if ultimately society adapts around step-function technological change. The best hedge against AI-powered capital overtaking labor is arguably to own more capital, whether through the S&P 500 or other vehicles.
Or one could raise the value of one's human capital, through training or becoming excellent at something. This has always been Warren Buffett's answer for how one should become inflation-resistant, as he detailed at Berkshire Hathaway's annual meeting a few years ago , at the height of the pandemic inflation surge.
Bull markets can keep rolling for a long while after they've become fully embraced and stocks are no longer cheap. But I find myself cataloguing various ways that the cushions against adverse surprises are getting worn pretty flat.
Here's the running tally of investors' collective cash holdings as a percentage of total margin debt. It's running well below the levels of the year 2000 at this point.

articles.title_orig: U.S. bans AI startup DeepSeek because of ‘threat vectors’ and China responds
articles.title_zh: U.S. bans AI startup DeepSeek because of ‘threat vectors’ and China responds
articles.content_orig:
Use of tools ‘may result in the transfer of sensitive data’ to China, defense department says
The US government on Monday ordered its agencies to stop using artificial intelligence (AI) tools from the Chinese startup DeepSeek , as the countries race for dominance in the fast-moving sector.
A notice from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) announced the ban on products developed by DeepSeek – and tools created using DeepSeek by third parties – saying they must be removed from IT devices.
The DHS can issue direction to civilian agencies but not the military or intelligence services. The US defense department did not respond to an AFP request for comment.
“DeepSeek’s models present multiple threat vectors,” said a document attached to Monday’s notice.
Use of DeepSeek AI tools “may result in the transfer of sensitive data to [China] if used by US government employees or vendors”, the department warned.
Its servers are located in China, where the legal system permits the government “extensive authority” to access private company infrastructure, it said.
DeepSeek has been contacted for comment.
One of China’s top AI labs, DeepSeek shook up the industry in January 2025 with a low-cost, high-performance chatbot, challenging assumptions of US dominance.
The firm released a long-awaited new model, V4, in April, and earlier in October updated a faster, more lightweight version of V4.
The US has accused DeepSeek and other top Chinese AI firms of systematically stealing the capabilities of cutting-edge models developed by American rivals.
Despite their fierce competition in the field, when their leaders Xi Jinping and Donald Trump met at the White House in September, China and the US agreed to set up a “communication channel” for AI incidents.
The topic is expected to arise again at a meeting between Xi and Trump at a summit scheduled for November in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.

articles.title_orig: UK to send jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks, and other Mideast news
articles.title_zh: UK to send jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks, and other Mideast news
articles.content_orig:
LONDON, Oct 20 (Reuters) – Britain will fly Royal Air Force Typhoon fighter jets on defensive missions to help protect Saudi cities and critical national infrastructure from Houthi aerial attacks , the Ministry of Defence said on Tuesday.
The ministry said the aircraft would operate only in a defensive role and would not conduct offensive strikes against the Iran-aligned Houthis, whose attacks Britain says threaten regional stability and risk disrupting energy supplies and trade routes.
“The continuing attacks from the Houthis on our ally Saudi Arabia are absolutely despicable. The targeting of the airport in Riyadh in particular shows the lengths the Houthis are going to escalate the situation in the region,” defense minister Wes Streeting said in a statement.
“That’s why today I have approved further UK military support. RAF Typhoons will fly defensive air missions to help protect Saudi airspace from drones and missiles.”
The additional support follows a request from Saudi Arabia’s government, which Prime Minister Andy Burnham said earlier this month Britain was prepared to consider.
Britain will also deploy an Atlas A400M transport aircraft and military advisers, expanding assistance announced in September which included an RAF Voyager air-to-air refueling aircraft but not fighter jets.
Houthi attacks against Saudi oil facilities and other infrastructure have intensified in recent weeks as the conflict in Yemen has escalated.
Inside Yemen, authorities said a Houthi strike on Monday against a training camp for Saudi-backed government security forces killed 58 people.

articles.title_orig: Zelenskyy meets with Trump envoys as U.S. blasts ‘scandalous’ accusations on withdrawn support
articles.title_zh: Zelenskyy meets with Trump envoys as U.S. blasts ‘scandalous’ accusations on withdrawn support
articles.content_orig:
U.S. envoys were meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Norway on Tuesday, as Kyiv scrambled to respond to an American pressure campaign that has been allied with moves aimed at courting the Kremlin.
President Donald Trump’s negotiators, son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff, have so far had little success finding a diplomatic solution to the war . Their latest meeting comes with Washington’s backing in doubt as Kyiv accused the U.S. of withdrawing support crucial to its defense against Russia — a suggestion that Secretary of State Marco Rubio called “scandalous.”
Witkoff had been set to meet with Zelenskyy in Oslo, with Kushner joining via videoconference, the Norwegian government said earlier. Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and Finnish President Alexander Stubb was also joining the talks, it added.
Officials from the U.S. and Ukraine had been expected to meet in Norway this week for another round of negotiations, sources familiar with the matter told NBC News, as a series of recent actions by Trump in favor of Russia left both Congress and U.S. allies questioning U.S. mediation efforts.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters he hoped that it would be possible for Trump’s envoys to hold a meeting in Russia “in the near future,” though he gave no firm indication on when this might be.
Trump has waived sanctions and agreed a diesel deal with Russia, in an apparent bid to lower fuel prices ahead of the Midterm elections. He called Monday for Zelenskyy to “get somebody else to negotiate,” his latest rebuke of the Ukrainian president.
Trump also appeared to downplay the impact of Russian attacks on Ukraine, a near-daily reality for the last 4 ½ years that have killed scores of civilians and flattened towns.
“Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine,” Trump told reporters. “They haven’t been doing much.”
It was the latest public sign of his shift away from Ukraine.
Kyiv said it had once again received no early warning from the U.S. before the capital came under attack by Russian ballistic missiles on Sunday, the third time in recent days.
In addition to the withholding of intelligence, Ukraine said it was still facing speed restrictions on Starshield, the military version of the SpaceX service, with no explanation from the American side.
“All of this suggests that some political decision has been made to slow down support for us,” Zelenskyy said Monday in a virtual address to a bipartisan Congressional delegation. He also said the U.S. was delaying the delivery of crucial ballistic missile interceptors, and that Ukraine has nearly run out of its supplies.
Zelenskyy said early Tuesday he held “a substantive conversation” with Rubio, focusing on missile interceptors, early warnings of ballistic attacks and Starshield restrictions. He thanked Rubio and “everyone in America who supports fair approaches.”
Rubio told reporters later that he told Zelenskyy in the 45-minute call that nothing had changed in U.S. support for Ukraine.
“There’s nothing being deliberately denied to Ukraine,” he added, speaking at the start of a trip to India.
When it comes to missile interceptors, Rubio said the U.S. has to strike a delicate balance between its obligations to other partners and its own requirements when it comes to what he called “the most in-demand product” in the defense industry right now.
“When a country doesn’t get interceptors from the United States, it’s not because we are denying,” he added. “We have our own needs too.”
Ukrainian officials including Zelenskyy have made clear their accusation that the U.S. has imposed restrictions that have disrupted military operations and hampered Ukraine’s ability to intercept Russian missiles, making the attacks more deadly.
“That’s scandalous, that’s outrageous, that’s just simply not true. That’s not accurate,” Rubio said Tuesday.
Officials in the eastern Kharkiv region shared images Monday of a dead child in a stroller — a one-year-old girl they said was killed alongside her mother in a Russian attack on a public park in the region.
“ The world has enough strength to stop the war. That strength must finally be used — against the murderers,” Zelenskyy said in a post decrying the strike.
Yuliya Talmazan is a reporter for NBC News Digital, based in London.
Abigail Williams is a producer and reporter for NBC News covering the State Department.

articles.title_zh: Over 1.5M pounds of meat recalled over serious potential health concerns
articles.content_orig:

A Massachusetts-based manufacturer has recalled more than 1.5 million pounds of various meat products over serious potential health concerns.
Kayem Foods Inc. initiated the recall after learning that the items may not have been stored at the correct temperature. It has since been deemed a Class I recall by the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service, meaning “there is a reasonable probability that the use of the product will cause serious, adverse health consequences or death.”
An investigation that began after a customer reported receiving a warm product delivery on October 1 revealed that a warehouse cooler experienced temperature fluctuations while storing the items, according to FSIS.
Approximately 1,584,361 recalled items were manufactured between March 31, 2026 and October 7, 2026 and are labeled with the establishment numbers “EST. M/P 7839,” “EST. P 20935A” or “EST. M 9520” inside the USDA inspection mark. Affected items were shipped to retail and food service locations across the U.S. and Hong Kong.
Products include various brands of hot dogs, bacon, sausage, and deli meat. A full list of affected items can be found here .
There have been no reports of illness, but customers in possession of recalled products should discard them or return them to the place of purchase.
The meat recall comes amid a slew of issues affecting consumers.
Over 112,000 bottles of pain relievers sold by Amazon were voluntarily recalled last week due to discoloration. The news was shared in an enforcement report from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration .
Various bottles of 500-milligram Extra Strength Acetaminophen caplets sold across the U.S. have been affected. Customer complaints about discolored tablets led to the voluntary recall initiated by Amazon, according to the report.
Included in the recall are 90,456 500-count bottles, 14,640 200-count bottles, and 7,836 1000-count bottles, all with various lot numbers and expiration dates between September 30, 2027 and February 29, 2028.
No injuries or adverse health effects related to the discoloration of the tablets have been reported.
Amazon has contacted customers who have purchased affected bottles for refund information. Customers can check their order history and product lot numbers on Amazon’s website .
A pre-workout powder has also been recalled after it was found to contain an illegal and dangerous stimulant , the FDA said last week.
A batch of “Leader Formulas, LLC RAPTURE Preworkout” sold online and in stores between January 2025 and May 2026 was made with “1,3-Dimethylamylamine,” also known as “ DMAA .”
DMAA is a synthetic chemical developed from amphetamine, sometimes used in dietary supplements that can spike blood pressure and lead to heart attacks, shortness of breath and tightening of the chest.

Episode two of the animated series Arkanaut lands on Warhammer TV on Friday! We’ll have more details on that and the official trailer on launch day, but here’s what else you can enjoy in the meantime.
The once-verdant muster world of Tallarn, with its vast network of defensible tunnels, became a target of the Traitor forces during the Horus Heresy , reduced to a desolate wasteland by the Iron Warriors .
However, thanks to the aforementioned tunnels, and the supplies within them, the people of Tallarn were able to launch a counterattack against the sons of Perturabo. In this episode, learn about Tallarn’s bleak history, the bitter fight for the planet, and how it played host to some of the largest tank battles in history.
The four contestants reach the 1,000-point milestone and are ready for battle once more in a series of Incursion-sized games with their fledgling Warhammer 40,000 armies. We hear from the warlords as they talk through their army lists, tactics and strategies, and lessons learned in victory and defeat.
Ultimate Paint-Off sees our trio of painters push themselves, and each other to the limit.
Our contestants must paint the largest model ever seen on Ultimate Paint-off – a Chaos Dragon from Warhammer: The Old World! While they have the full Warhammer Tone Pro paint range at their disposal, they only have the new Warhammer Pro Tone dry brushes to apply it with.
If you’re inspired by the use of the new Tone Pro paints, don’t forget that they will be available in-store from Saturday!
As mentioned, episode 2 of Arkanaut is out on Friday. Captain Orra and her crew have claimed their prize – a Stormcast soul – and now they must defend it! Come back on Friday for more behind-the-scenes details from episode 2.
Also available on Friday is the epic original score of the Horus Heresy animation Kill Lupercal – perfect for soundtracking your weekend’s activities. It joins a range of soundtracks from other Warhammer TV animations, including Aeronautica Imperialis , Adepta Sororitas: Penitence , and more.
This week’s episodes join an immense back catalogue of over 700 episodes of gaming shows, hobby guides, animations, and more. Your subscription also unlocks expanded features in the Warhammer 40,000 and Warhammer Age of Sigmar apps, access to years of lore books and magazines in the Warhammer Vault , automatic entry into regular competitions, and even a pair of special subscriber-only miniatures and the Warhammer Yearbook when you sign up for a whole year. You’ll also get 12 months for the price of nine when you sign up for an annual subscription.

articles.title_orig: Apple explains why HomeView couldn’t launch until now
articles.title_zh: Apple explains why HomeView couldn’t launch until now
articles.content_orig:
Apple’s new HomeView was reportedly mostly finished for years, but kept getting delayed. Here’s why HomeView couldn’t launch until now, per quotes from key Apple execs.
In November 2024, Mark Gurman published an in-depth report on the product we now know as HomeView. At the time, he said Apple was targeting a March 2025 launch. But that date kept slipping, and now HomeView will finally arrive in homes on November 13, 2026.
Why the long wait? Gurman has repeatedly pointed to Siri AI as the chief cause of delays. And Apple execs have now largely confirmed that in quotes given to The Verge .
Jennifer Pattison Tuohy asked Kaiann Drance, Apple’s VP of product marketing for home, why now was the right time for HomeView and Apple’s renewed smart home push.
She said Siri AI and the personal context it brings, which she called Apple’s “privacy story,” came together with a device designed specifically for the home. “With the magic of Siri AI, it comes together in a way that we haven’t been able to deliver before,” she said.
HomeView is being marketed as a shared device that taps into users’ personal context in a way that wasn’t possible pre-Siri AI. So it’s easy to see how Apple’s main pitch would need to change without the more personalized Siri.
A similar explanation was given by Apple’s Lilian Rincon, VP of product marketing for AI. She told The Verge that Siri AI is core to HomeView because it’s “much more capable” and also highlighted its conversational abilities, which make it easy to use for any family member.
“It’s great because you can just ask it to change the temperature on your thermostat in a very natural way. As the Siri AI capabilities continue to evolve, the home experience is fitting to be able to interact with in this natural way.” On why now, Rincon says the natural-language shift is the point where AI goes mainstream. “Because now it can be … my mother-in-law or the Gen Z who’s in college, both of them can use this in the way that they naturally speak and get what they want.”
This emphasis and explanation also makes HomeView’s absence in the EU more understandable.
If Siri AI was simply a nice-to-have addition to an otherwise feature-rich product, perhaps it could launch in the EU still. But if the whole value proposition revolves around the new assistant and its personalized features, waiting until Siri AI is available for iOS in the EU makes more sense.
You can read The Verge’s full article here for more quotes and context.

articles.title_orig: Google Says Services Are Recovering After U.K. Cloud Outage Hits Businesses
articles.title_zh: Google Says Services Are Recovering After U.K. Cloud Outage Hits Businesses
articles.content_orig:
Multiple Google Cloud services experienced disruptions in the company’s London region on Tuesday, according to its service status page, while British digital bank Revolut also reported a service outage.
“Multiple Google Cloud services are experiencing elevated errors and intermittent network failures in europe-west2 region,” Google said on its website, referring to the London region. The issues began just after 7 a.m. local time, the company said.
“We apologize to all who are affected by the disruption,” it added.
Shortly after 1 p.m. local time, Google said it was “seeing the recovery of services” across most of the region. The company also said that “power event” had caused the outage in part of the London area.
A Google spokesperson said in a statement that the company was investigating the issue.
Revolut said on its website that several of its services were partially unavailable, including card payments, topping up balances via bank cards, ATM withdrawals and currency exchange.
A person familiar with the matter told Reuters that Revolut’s service outage was related to the Google Cloud service disruption.
“We are currently experiencing a service disruption affecting multiple services. We can confirm that all our customers’ money and data are safe,” Revolut said on X.
Google said its engineering team was investigating the issue, which impacted the London-based data center.
Multiple websites and apps experienced disruptions on Tuesday, including banks HSBC, Barclays and Lloyds Bank, according to Downdetector, a website tracking user reports of service disruptions. But it is not clear whether the Google Cloud outage was behind those issues.
Separately, ING Germany said there were problems logging into online banking and its banking app due to a technical issue.
The outage “is a reminder of how deeply our economies depend on just a handful of cloud providers,” Feng Li, associate dean for research and innovation at Bayes Business School at City St George’s, University of London. “A problem in one region can interrupt banking, payments and other services well beyond the provider itself.”
This story and headline have been updated with additional reporting.
Hanna Ziady and Maisie Linford contributed reporting.

tvOS 27.2 is coming next week, bringing several new features to Apple TV 4K users—including some screen saver upgrades. Here’s what’s new.
tvOS offers a variety of great screen savers across multiple categories, including Aerials, Memories & Slideshows, Portraits, and Snoopy.
But historically, you’ve had to choose just one of these categories for your Apple TV screen savers, thus missing out on all the others.
In tvOS 27.2, Apple has a new ‘Shuffle’ option which will cycle through all available screen savers—regardless of category—throughout the day.
I’ve always favored Apple’s beautiful selection of Aerials. But I love that now I can continue enjoying Aerials while also benefiting from the other screen saver categories too.

If you want to curate Photos screen savers, tvOS 27.2 lets you do that in a new and convenient way.

articles.title_orig: Australian MP hit by vehicle has leg amputated - as suspect's father says she is family friend
articles.title_zh: Australian MP hit by vehicle has leg amputated - as suspect's father says she is family friend
articles.content_orig:
A 43-year-old man has been charged after Australian MP Helen Haines was hit by a car in the state of Victoria on Monday.
The suspect will appear in court on Wednesday to face charges of dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury and the federal offence of causing harm to a public official.
Local media earlier named the alleged attacker as environmental activist Brendan Nugent. His father and his partner said they had been friends with Haines "for more than 20 years" and thanked residents and officers who helped her after the "shocking and horrific crime".
Haines remains in a critical condition after surgery and is reported to have lost one of her legs.
"Helen Haines is a deeply respected, valued and much loved member of our local community," Rod Nugent and his partner Christine Cunningham said in a statement.
"All of our love and all of our thoughts are with Helen and her family and friends."
They promised to assist Victoria Police "in any way we can".
Police say they will allege the incident was targeted.
Haines, 65, the independent member for Indi, is in a critical but stable condition after undergoing surgery at a Melbourne hospital.
She was airlifted there after bystanders rushed to help.
A local barber who was there says he pulled the suspect out of his car.
"I don't think I'm a hero. I think that I was just a person who had an opportunity to intervene in a safe-ish way," said Ricky Jefferies.
Others who helped "didn't even check for danger", he added. "The car was still on and they sat in front of a rolling car, that's not an exaggeration."
In their statement, Victoria Police say a highway patrol unit was nearby at the time of the incident and "on scene" within eight seconds of the call coming through.
As they announced the charges against the 43-year-old, they said they had searched a property in Tarrawingee, around 12km (7.5 miles) from Wangaratta.
"At this stage it appears this is an isolated incident, and there are currently no other known threats connected to this matter," they said, adding officers would maintain a presence in Wangaratta.
Haines won the seat of Indi as an independent in 2019, and has since become a prominent member of the crossbench, building rapport across Australia's increasingly divided political spectrum.
The community, and country, remain in shock.
At a vigil on Tuesday, locals queued patiently in the aisle of the Holy Trinity Cathedral, waiting for their turn to light a candle. Priests hugged some of those who came to pay their respects.
Wangaratta's main street, where Haines's office is located, had reopened to traffic. Cars slowly filed past the growing number of bouquets being left for her on the pavement.
One card read: "May you recover quickly and continue to be a light in this world."

articles.title_orig: China slams US ban on DeepSeek AI over security concerns
articles.title_zh: China slams US ban on DeepSeek AI over security concerns
articles.content_orig:
Boeing unveiled a new artificial intelligence-powered platform Tuesday designed to help airlines anticipate aircraft maintenance needs, identify emerging risks and make faster operational decisions using data collected across their fleets.
The platform, called Dataliner, was developed in partnership with Microsoft and uses AI to combine aircraft maintenance records, operational information and Boeing's engineering expertise to give airlines a more complete picture of their fleets.
Built using Microsoft's Azure AI Foundry and other technologies, Dataliner aims to help airlines move beyond analyzing individual aircraft to identifying maintenance trends and potential problems across entire fleets.
"Airlines have more data available to them than ever before, but turning that data into meaningful action remains a challenge," said Lindsey Douglas, vice president of Cabin, Modifications, Maintenance and Digital Services at Boeing Global Services.
Douglas said the platform will help customers "anticipate maintenance needs, identify emerging risks and take timely action."
Boeing said airlines will retain control over their data, including what information they share, while the platform uses encryption, access controls and monitoring to protect sensitive aviation information.
Dataliner will also support the development of new Boeing digital services, including an AI-powered tool for airline technical operations and aircraft lifecycle planning.
China demanded Tuesday that the Trump administration reverse its ban on Chinese artificial intelligence startup DeepSeek across federal civilian agencies, warning that Beijing would take "all necessary measures" to protect its interests.
China's Commerce Ministry accused Washington of disregarding understandings reached between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, urging the U.S. to "immediately correct wrong practices ... and revoke relevant discriminatory restrictive measures," according to Reuters.
Beijing said it was "strongly dissatisfied and firmly opposes" the ban, calling on Washington to honor the consensus reached between the two leaders and make full use of an existing U.S.-China artificial intelligence dialogue mechanism.
The Department of Homeland Security ordered federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek products and third-party services developed using its AI models from government IT systems, while also prohibiting future purchases.
DHS cited national security concerns, warning that DeepSeek's models pose "multiple threat vectors" and could expose sensitive U.S. data to Chinese authorities.
Reuters contributed to this report.
China launched a new state-owned data enterprise Tuesday aimed at strengthening its position in the global artificial intelligence race as Beijing moves to expand the development and use of data resources critical to advancing AI technology.
The National Data Group, headquartered in Xiongan, roughly 60 miles southwest of Beijing, will serve as a national platform to promote data sharing across industries and regions, according to state media.
The group will also work with various stakeholders to develop China's data economy, explore new business models and expand the market, state broadcaster CCTV reported.
Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang attended Tuesday's inauguration ceremony, saying the group's establishment was important for capitalizing on opportunities in artificial intelligence and strengthening China's competitive edge, according to state media.
The announcement comes amid intensifying technological competition between Washington and Beijing, including a recent U.S. ban on Chinese AI startup DeepSeek's products across federal civilian agencies over national security concerns.
China established its National Data Administration in 2023 to oversee data policy, while the new National Data Group will focus on market operations and putting data resources to use.
Reuters contributed to this report.
Artificial intelligence may be transforming the job market, but nearly half of U.S. employers believe the technology will make college degrees more valuable over the next five years, according to a new Gallup poll.
The Gallup-Lumina Foundation survey found that 48% of employers expect AI to increase the importance of college degrees, compared with 26% who believe the technology will make them less valuable.
The findings suggest higher education remains a priority for hiring managers despite growing concerns about AI's impact on the workforce.
About 80% of employers said they prefer hiring candidates with college degrees, even for positions that do not require one.
The survey also revealed a divide between employers and the broader public over the value of higher education.
While 60% of employers expressed a great deal or quite a lot of confidence in higher education, just 38% of U.S. adults reported the same in a separate Gallup survey conducted in June.
The findings are based on an August survey of 2,500 U.S. hiring decision-makers.
Pharmaceutical giant AstraZeneca is teaming up with tech powerhouse Oracle to use artificial intelligence to identify patients for clinical trials and monitor potential safety risks, in a move aimed at speeding up drug development and improving medical research.
The partnership will combine AstraZeneca's drug development expertise with Oracle's AI technology and healthcare data capabilities to help researchers match patients with clinical trials and identify potential safety concerns.
The collaboration will initially focus on cancer, cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, immunology and rare diseases, with the technology potentially helping doctors diagnose serious illnesses earlier.
AstraZeneca CEO Pascal Soriot said the partnership could help researchers and healthcare providers improve patient care through AI-driven technology.
"We can help clinicians identify patients sooner, optimize clinical trials, and generate evidence continuously across the lifecycle of a medicine," Soriot said in a statement.
The first project will focus on hypertension research in Abu Dhabi, in partnership with UAE-based healthcare company M42.
Patient recruitment remains a major obstacle in clinical research, with enrollment delays often extending trial timelines and driving up development costs.
AstraZeneca has also faced clinical trial setbacks, including delays involving a breast cancer treatment and the failure of a nerve disorder drug, raising concerns about its drug development efforts, according to Reuters.
The companies have signed a non-binding agreement and have not disclosed financial terms.
The partnership comes as AstraZeneca seeks to expand its drug portfolio and reach more than $80 billion in annual revenue by 2030.
Reuters contributed to this report.
China fired back at the Trump administration Tuesday after the U.S. government ordered federal civilian agencies to remove Chinese artificial intelligence startup DeepSeek's products from their systems, citing national security concerns and the risk that Beijing could gain access to sensitive American data.
The Department of Homeland Security ordered agencies to remove DeepSeek products and services, including third-party technology developed using its AI models, and prohibited future purchases, according to a notice made public Monday in the Federal Register.
The order, issued in July, warned that DeepSeek's AI models "present multiple threat vectors," citing concerns that the company's China-based servers could potentially expose sensitive U.S. data to Chinese authorities.
Beijing criticized the ban, with Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning accusing Washington of politicizing technology.
"China consistently opposes the overstretching of the concept of national security and the politicizing of science, technology, economic and trade issues," Mao told reporters Tuesday.
Mao added that Beijing would "resolutely safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies.

articles.title_orig: Oil prices move higher as traders adjust to a new normal in the Middle East
articles.title_zh: Oil prices move higher as traders adjust to a new normal in the Middle East
articles.content_orig:
Oil prices surged in early trading Tuesday, as energy markets adjusted to a new normal in the Middle East. The increase in crude prices threatened to drive up the cost of gas in the United States just two weeks before the midterm elections.
U.S. crude prices jumped as much as 5% to about $109 a barrel, the highest price since April, while the price of international Brent crude climbed 1.5% to more than $111, its highest price since May. Prices pulled back later in the morning, after weaker-than-expected U.S. housing starts raised the prospect of a broader slowdown and lower demand.
Prices for advanced oil contracts dated for next year also hit record highs , “implying an extended period of high oil prices deep into 2027,” Deutsche Bank analysts said in a note Tuesday.
“The 2027 contracts are moving higher as well as the possible reality of higher for longer oil prices sink in,” Peter Boockvar, author of the Boock Report and chief investment officer of OnePoint BFG Wealth Partners, said in a note Tuesday.
High gas prices have become a major issue for voters in the midterms, where Republicans face dwindling odds of maintaining their control of Congress.
A recent NBC News poll found that 67% of U.S. adults believe gas prices are a “very serious” or “somewhat serious” problem. A majority also said that current economic conditions have caused them to change their spending habits.
U.S. gasoline prices had started off the week lower. At $4.28 a gallon, the national average price of unleaded was on pace to reach its lowest level in a month.
But that trend is likely to be upended as higher crude prices filter through to the pump.
Several factors were contributing to Tuesday’s oil price hikes.
The cost of chartering a large tanker vessel to transport oil through the Strait of Hormuz has quadrupled since September, data shows.
Much of that increase is a risk premium, both for sailors and insurance. During the past two weeks, at least 18 ⁠vessels have been attacked in the strait, the ship-tracking group Kpler said in a note ⁠Monday.
The higher cost of transport has begun to offset the recent bump in supply from a growing number of ships moving through the strait.
The Iranian attacks on ships have also prompted investor speculation that the Trump administration will be more likely to escalate against Iran after the midterms, the Deutsche Bank analysts said.
Iran-aligned Houthi rebels also claimed Monday that they had hit airport, energy and military targets in Saudi Arabia, as well as a ​training camp in Yemen for that government’s security forces.
The U.K. will begin deploying fighter jets over Saudi Arabia to help protect against further Houthi attacks, the Defense Ministry said Tuesday.
The entry of another country’s military into the regional hostilities was taken as a further sign of escalating tensions.
Rob Wile is a Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist covering breaking business stories for NBCNews.com.

articles.title_orig: Walmart rolls out new bundle combining Walmart+, Sam’s Club Plus
articles.title_zh: Walmart rolls out new bundle combining Walmart+, Sam’s Club Plus
articles.content_orig:
LSEG head of consumer research Jharonne Marti discusses the mind of the consumer and the Walmart overreaction on 'Making Money.'
Walmart announced Tuesday it is rolling out a new membership bundle that gives shoppers access to both Walmart+ and Sam’s Club Plus for $120 a year, nearly $100 less than purchasing the two memberships separately.
The bundle works out to the equivalent of $10 per month, though Walmart said it will only be available as an annual membership and will not include a monthly option or free trial.
Walmart CEO John Furner told FOX Business that the retail giant wanted to roll out the combined membership ahead of the holiday season, when many households are looking for ways to save both money and time.
"It does help at a time when we do see some customers showing some signs of pressure," Furner said, pointing in particular to higher energy costs.
SAM’S CLUB EXPANDS THANKSGIVING MEAL, KEEPING COST UNDER $10 A PERSON AS INFLATION WEIGHS ON CONSUMERS
Walmart said the combined membership costs almost $100 less annually than paying for Walmart+ and Sam’s Club Plus separately. (Christopher Dilts/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
The launch comes after Walmart reported continued growth across its membership and e-commerce businesses in its most recent quarterly results in August.
During the company's second-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings call on Aug. 20, Furner said membership fee revenue increased 17% to an all-time high.
"Marketplace, fulfillment services, membership, advertising and other commerce solutions are strengthening our business, and they are improving the economics of the company," he said at the time.
WALMART DOUBLES DOWN ON PLEDGE AGAINST AI-POWERED PERSONALIZED PRICING
Furner also said Walmart+ membership grew by double digits during the quarter, while Sam's Club membership posted growth in the U.S., China and Mexico.
He told FOX Business that the bundle is designed to appeal across income levels.
WALMART EXPANDS DRONE DELIVERY TO 2 MAJOR US CITIES
Walmart+ currently costs $98 for the standard annual plan, while Sam's Club Plus costs $120 a year.
The new bundle rivals Amazon Prime, which costs $139 annually.
Members will receive the benefits of both programs, including free delivery from Walmart and Sam’s Club, access to Sam’s Club locations and member-only pricing, a choice between Peacock and Paramount+, gas discounts and 2% Sam’s Cash on eligible purchases, according to the retailer.
Furner said Walmart aims to have the bundle encourage existing Walmart+ members to shop at Sam’s Club and also appeal to consumers who currently have memberships elsewhere.
"We're deciding to do this from a position of strength and momentum," Furner said.
Annual Walmart+ members can add Sam’s Club Plus for an additional $22 per year, while existing Sam’s Club members can upgrade to Plus for $60 and receive Walmart+ at no additional cost.
Current Sam’s Club Plus members will be able to activate Walmart+ at no additional charge.
Inflation accelerated in September, with higher energy costs helping push consumer prices higher. (Scott Olson/Getty Images)
Walmart also said U.S. field associates at Walmart and Sam’s Club will receive access to both memberships as part of their employee benefits.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The new offering comes as consumers continue to contend with higher prices. Inflation climbed 3.7% in September from a year earlier, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics' Consumer Price Index. Gasoline prices rose more than 34% over the past year, while grocery prices climbed 1.8%.

articles.title_orig: Russia is working 'closely' with Iran as Qatar says US-Tehran talks are still on
articles.title_zh: Russia is working 'closely' with Iran as Qatar says US-Tehran talks are still on
articles.content_orig:
Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesperson says "We are working with Washington and Tehran in partnership with other mediating countries to end the war in the region"
Qatar's public positioning as an intermediary between Washington and Tehran fits an established pattern: Doha has repeatedly served as a back-channel in Gulf and nuclear-related disputes, typically acting where larger powers lack direct lines. Statements of this kind from a foreign ministry spokesperson are an early-stage signal, and episodes of this sort have tended to run a long sequence from shuttle contacts and indirect messaging to any actual cessation framework, with most stalling before a formal outcome. The mechanism that matters for pricing is whether mediation language is corroborated by the principals, since crude's geopolitical premium and Gulf freight and insurance costs have historically retraced on confirmed de-escalation steps and re-emerged when talks were disavowed. The distinction worth drawing is between a ceasefire track and a broader settlement track; the former tends to compress risk premium quickly, the latter drags. Worth watching is whether Washington or Tehran echo the framing, any movement in front-month crude relative to the back of the curve, and whether parallel mediators such as Oman surface, which in past episodes has marked a more serious round.

articles.title_orig: SpaceX earnings live updates: Starlink growth, AI revenue and merger speculation
articles.title_zh: SpaceX earnings live updates: Starlink growth, AI revenue and merger speculation
articles.content_orig:
SpaceX is set to announce third-quarter results after the bell on Tuesday, the second earnings report for Elon Musk's defense tech conglomerate since its record IPO in June.
Here's what analysts are expecting, according to LSEG consensus estimates:
While SpaceX is best known for its reusable rockets, most of its revenue and profit in recent quarters came from the company's connectivity segment, which consists of its Starlink satellite internet service.
Buzz is building about Starlink's plans to build a U.S. network after SpaceX, earlier this month, announced that it's buying 800 MHz of low-band spectrum, and after the Federal Communications Commission approved a plan for the company to build out a 15,000-satellite constellation.
The moves strengthen "Starlink Mobile's ability to compete with major carriers by enabling broader, deeper coverage," RBC Capital Markets analysts wrote in a note ahead of earnings. The firm has a $225 price target on SpaceX stock and the equivalent of a buy rating.
In the third quarter, analysts are expecting AI revenue of $6.47 billion, connectivity sales of $4.84 billion, and revenue in the space business of $1.41 billion, according to StreetAccount.
During the third quarter, SpaceX also closed its $60 billion purchase of AI coding startup Cursor.
What you need to know ahead of the earnings report:
In its first earnings report in August, SpaceX reported capital expenditures of $18.4 billion, with 80% of that going towards its artificial intelligence division.
That number spooked Wall Street, and shares dropped following the report.
SpaceX and xAI merged in February and the company has been pouring money into its effort to become a major player in AI, a market dominated by OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. The AI division also acquired Cursor in a $60 billion transaction and is now known as either SpaceXAI or SpaceXSI, with the "SI" standing for President Donald Trump's preferred "Super Intelligence."
Wall Street is sounding bullish on SpaceX ahead of its third-quarter earnings report, to be delivered after the bell on Tuesday.
Mizuho has an outperform rating on the stock and a $200 price target, per a Monday note from analyst Brett Linzey. Shares were trading around $148 as of 10:45 a.m. on Tuesday.
"AI is the largest swing factor for 3Q26 revenue and EBITDA. Consensus has AI revenue of $6.30B (+146% Q/Q from $2.56B) and AI adj. EBITDA of $3.32B (from $1.15B)," he wrote.
Analysts are expecting some conversation about deals or competitive plays with cable and telecom companies following SpaceX's acquisition of low-band spectrum earlier this month.
"We expect initial strategic commentary centers around Connectivity and how SPCX can partner/compete its way into global markets, although we think low-band distribution becomes a meaningful intelligence lever over time," Colin Canfield at Cantor Fitzgerald wrote in a Monday note. He has a price target of $246 and an overweight rating on the stock.
Oppenheimer's expectations are more measured. The bank thinks the quarter will be "in-line" with "guidance reiterated."
"Industry subscriber growth is slowing with limited room for pricing action, so focus is shifting from net adds and service revenue growth toward cost-cutting using AI, and lower subsidies/churn," Timothy Horan at Oppenheimer told clients in a Tuesday note. He expects "more rational incumbent behavior" from SpaceX's competitors.
Musk said Monday that he'll give every child in the U.S. one of his SpaceX shares next year.
With 72 million children under 18 in the U.S. as of July 1, 2025, according to official census data, that would amount a giveaway of about $10.5 billion worth of shares as of the current price.
Musk, the world's richest person with a net worth of over $900 billion, said in a post on X that, "This will be the first of many," without providing further details. However, when it comes to fulfilling his philanthropic promises , Musk has a spotty track record.
A military tier of Starlink, marketed as Starshield, has drawn scrutiny of late as restrictions on the system in Ukraine hindered the country's ability to defend itself against intensifying attacks by Russia.
Ukrainian officials said SpaceX and the Trump administration restricted Starshield without warning last week, causing Ukraine's military forces to lose control of drones moving over 100 miles per hour, as the craft were relying on Starshield for connectivity at those speeds.
Musk said in a post on X that any changes to Starshield should be attributed to the U.S. government and President Donald Trump, though Trump later denied he ordered any such restrictions.
Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told NBC's "Meet the Press" on Sunday that the restraints remained in place over the weekend.
Investors, meanwhile, have poured capital into potential Starlink competitors, including Eutelsat .
After acquiring xAI in February with its data centers in and around Memphis, Tennessee, SpaceX struck lucrative cloud computing agreements, establishing a new revenue stream.
Deals with Google, Anthropic and Reflection AI, as well as an unnamed customer revealed by SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen at an event last month, amount to potentially tens of billions of dollars in annual revenue for the company.
SpaceX is reportedly in talks to raise up to $40 billion to buy more Nvidia chips to support its AI ambitions.
Investors are looking for updates around this business for SpaceX as it seeks to monetize its AI capacity.
Ahead of earnings, investors are invited to submit questions for the call. One entry that got a lot of upvotes was about timing for a potential merger between SpaceX and Tesla, Musk's automaker.
Musk's companies have had business and financial relations for years, even sharing personnel and some board members.
Tesla invested $2 billion into xAI, which later converted into shares of SpaceX. The AI unit of SpaceX also spent about $430 million last year on Tesla's Megapacks, which are battery energy storage systems, and $143 million on Cybertrucks.
With SpaceX hitting the public market in June, speculation about a more permanet tie-up has been swirling. SpaceX COO Gwynne Shotwell told CNBC ahead of the IPO that a merger "might make Elon's life a little easier."
A demo of Tesla's next-generation Roadster last week stirred up further merger excitement among Musk fans. The new Roadster was developed with SpaceX and incorporates its technology, including cold gas thrusters, to enable the car to launch, hover and flip in mid-air.

articles.title_orig: Final Fantasy dips back into the SNES golden era with Resonance
articles.title_zh: Final Fantasy dips back into the SNES golden era with Resonance
articles.content_orig:
To evoke the classics is also to hold yourself to the high standard set by them. With Final Fantasy Resonance bringing the venerated series back to its origins with turn-based combat, and wielding Square’s HD-2D art style to modernize nostalgia for the pixel art era, it plucks at something I've longed for as someone who grew up in the SNES generation. While I've expressed my love for the Octopath Traveler series time and again, Final Fantasy has of course crystalized into something meaningful over the past several decades. But as much as Resonance looks like a torchbearer for classic RPGs, it also goes for a style of storytelling that often rings hollow. So, I think of it as a game of moments – when a genre-fusing boss theme graces your ears, when you execute a turn perfectly and watch all your spells fire off with big damage numbers, and when a cutscene brings HD-2D to life in a way you've just never seen before.
Resonance adapts the story and characters from the now-shuttered mobile game Final Fantasy: Brave Exvius by packaging them into the structure of a traditional RPG; no gacha mechanics, no microtransactions. It's quite similar to what Square Enix did with Octopath Traveler 0 and it's a brilliant way to bring existing stories into a format I'm a lot more inclined to play. With that comes an overworld with towns to represent each region, random encounters, an airship for roaming free and discovering pieces of land that feel like secrets, and full voice acting throughout the main story.
It largely sticks to the events of the first season of Brave Exvius, which follows the knights from the Kingdom of Grandshelt, Rain and Laswell, the mysterious magical girl born from a crystal, Fina, along with additional friends on a quest to stop the armor-clad Sworn Six from destroying the world's crystals and plunging it into calamity. Of course, there's more beneath the surface. That said, a lot of dialogue and interstitial events have been added to fill out the journey, which took me about 45 hours to complete (including all of the side quests marked on my map and poking around the overworld for optional minibosses who offer intense challenges). While chunks of Resonance's story aren't very riveting, the production value here had me forgetting that this was built on the bones of a mobile game – not that Brave Exvius was any lesser of an achievement for what it was.
That retooling extends to gameplay, which retains concepts and mechanics that work extremely well as an engaging turn-based combat system – and hearing "turn-based" and Final Fantasy in the same breath after all these years released those good chemicals in my brain, too. This is not an ATB system with an active element, but a straightforward turn order along a timeline. And the way you either plan accordingly depending on which units are up or manipulate the order to your advantage had me employing similar strategies as I do in the Trails series or the Octopath Traveler games.
It's all about elemental affinities and staggering enemies in Resonance, however. Each party member has their own set of elements covered through magic spells or element-imbued physical attacks, but they also equip what are called Visions that function somewhat like a Job system directly inspired by Final Fantasy V. This is what provides flexibility in party composition, giving you the tools to make sure you either cover all the elements or go all-in on a specific type so you can streamroll bosses. While every attack chips at an enemy's stagger meter, hitting their weaknesses is, of course, the strategy demanded of you.
I'm of two minds with this system: while it’s nice to have flexibility as you swap Visions between party members to constantly change their overall movesets, it can sometimes trivialize your combat approach. For example, going into a water-themed boss fight, I knew purely electric builds were going to be the optimal strategy. So, while it was rad as hell to watch chunks of stagger and HP get chopped off as I spammed electric attacks, I often didn't feel the need to think much harder than that. Having the foresight to anticipate the right element before a fight isn't quite as rewarding as being pushed to scheme with what you have.
Compare this to the boost and break system of an Octopath Traveler, where the tools you're given are more dynamic and free-flowing even with elemental affinities involved, which then lets you get more creative rather than just having you hammer away with one specific element. I cruised through the first half of Resonance since most enemies and bosses were pushovers. But thankfully, things got tougher in the late game where they hit harder and inflicted more status ailments to work around. Key moments where I was challenged to think steps ahead culminated in some real hard-fought battles toward the end.
Overall, it still provides enough of the puzzle-esque tactical thinking that's required of a good turn-based RPG. Party members level up alongside their mastery of equipped Visions, but you have to manually rank up Visions then apply passive perks and support spells, which gets into some interesting buildcrafting that gives a little extra depth that mattered for those big fights. And I enjoyed Resonance's combat system because it still captures the satisfaction of teeing off on a staggered enemy with your nastiest spells, especially because their animations look so good and hit with emphatic impact.
Visions themselves are super fun to toy with because most of them are avatars of star characters from Final Fantasy's past. Their movesets call back to specific spells and signature attacks from their respective games, and it's nice to see parts of the series' history celebrated in a way that's integral to how Resonance plays. Staggering an enemy grants extra turns in a bonus phase, and staggering all of them (or a lone foe) leads to the sweeping stagger phase where everyone gets to pile on, which then concludes in a Resonance attack tied to a Vision of your choosing. I still find it jarring to go from beautiful HD-2D to a CGI cutscene (pulled from Brave Exvius) when summoning a Resonance attack, some of these are pretty cool, like big Shanttoto throwing a massive boulder of dark energy or Clive getting ready to hit L3+R3 to accept the truth. There's some wonderful pixel art around those cuts that look incredible, too, like Lightning, who gets a full animation set here – and it's lovely to see these characters recreated in that style.
Each is obtained by visiting shrines sprinkled throughout the overworld and going through a quiz-like dialogue sequence that walks through the events of their own stories (and beware, there are some major spoilers for Final Fantasies you have not played yet). I found this pretty cheesy at first, but it really grew on me as a reminder of how each entry captured something powerful that has stood the test of time. You never really know which shrine belongs to who, so when their music kicks in, it had me grinning ear-to-ear – and as someone who was deeply touched by FFXIV Shadowbringers, hearing "Tomorrow and Tomorrow" and recounting Y'shtola's ongoing story is a prime example of how sometimes Resonance got me.
More than the hard-fought battles against god-like beings, Final Fantasy has stuck around and won our hearts because of the stories it tells. And this is where I wrestled most with Resonance. The foundations of its story are quite solid and consistent as a classic Final Fantasy about the power of crystals that fuel these magical worlds and defeating evil to save the world against villains who reveal themselves to be more complicated by story's end. But it's always about how those stories get told and the impactful themes they explore along the way. Resonance has glimpses of hitting those same highs, yet I found long stretches of its storytelling to be quite underwhelming.
Taking the story of Brave Exvius and expanding on it was definitely worth exploring

articles.title_orig: France Protests Show Europe’s Shift Away From Centrist Politics
articles.title_zh: France Protests Show Europe’s Shift Away From Centrist Politics
articles.content_orig:
Anger over the cost of living and pressure on public services has brought hundreds of thousands of protesters onto streets across several European countries, with grievances ranging from expensive housing to poor conditions in schools and universities.
France saw the largest demonstrations at the weekend, with more than 500,000 people marching. Most protested peacefully, but some looted and vandalized shops, set fire to city halls and attacked police officers.
Separate protests also took place in Italy, Spain, Portugal and Albania on Saturday and Sunday. Their immediate triggers differed, although high fuel and energy costs formed part of the backdrop in several countries. The wars in Iran and Ukraine have pushed diesel prices sharply higher across the continent.
There's no one "single trigger" for the riots, Capital Economics' Chief Europe Economist Andrew Kenningham told CNBC. The increase in energy costs may be playing a role, but the increase is smaller than in 2022, at the onset of the Russia-Ukraine war, when there were no comparable violent protests, he added.
Nevertheless, the demonstrations pose a shared challenge for governments: how to improve living conditions and maintain public services while supporting households and keeping strained public finances in check.
The demonstrations in France began last month when high school students criticized poor schooling conditions, including shoddy facilities and teacher shortages. They have since evolved into broader protests over living standards and declining public services.
In Spain, housing protests began in September after an 87-year-old woman, Maricarmen Abascal, was evicted following a 230% rent increase by an investment fund. She died a fortnight later.
Thousands of protesters also took to the streets in Portugal on Saturday to demonstrate against soaring housing costs and the cost of living.
"People obviously are protesting on the cost of living with diesel and fuel prices, but mainly on housing costs, which have been increasing substantially all over Europe, but also particularly in Portugal," Miranda Sarmento, Portugal's minister of state and finance, said Monday.
In Albania, protesters were angry about poor university conditions and high tuition fees, and called for the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama. Some threw Molotov cocktails and other objects at the police and set fire to cars and litter bins.
In Italy, a march in central Milan on Saturday over living costs also ended violently, with rioters attacking the police with stones and paving blocks and setting fire to barricades.
"The underlying problem is that politicians are not able to offer hope of a better life for many Europeans because the economy is growing only slowly and governments have built up huge debts, leaving them little scope to support higher public spending or to cut taxes," Capital Economics' Kenningham said.
The escalation of violence in France in particular is due to a "conjugation of different elements," said Douglas Yates, a professor at the American Graduate School in Paris.
"This was a storm that turned into a hurricane," Yates told CNBC's Steve Sedgwick. "There was this inflation, which has brought out the cost-of-living protesters who would have been disgruntled at any rate."
Yates said another factor is France's 2027 presidential election, as opposition parties seek to capitalize on growing public discontent with President Emmanuel Macron .
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has proposed a 2027 budget aimed at narrowing France's deficit , projected at 5.4% of gross domestic product this year. Measures include freezing the civil service pay index and tightening reimbursement for sick leave.
"Finally there's the students, the poor students who started this by making reasonable demands for having their dilapidated infrastructure repaired and perhaps getting some air conditioners installed in the classrooms, and so these three forces have come together and created an out-of-control hurricane," Yates added.
The economic backdrop has also deteriorated. In the second quarter of 2026, France's unemployment rate rose to 8.3%, representing 2.7 million people, according to Insee, the national statistics bureau . The unemployment rate among 15- to 24-year-olds climbed to 21.6%.
Consumer prices rose 3.1% in September from a year earlier, up from 2.4% in August, according to final Insee data. Energy prices jumped 21.3%. Meanwhile, purchasing power per consumption unit is projected to fall 0.7% in 2026, according to Insee figures, cited by Le Monde .
Calculations by the French Institute of Economics for Le Monde estimate that the decline in purchasing power since 2024 is equivalent to a loss of 1,200 euros ($1,345) a year for a household with two adults and two children, and 600 euros for a single adult.
Portugal's Sarmento said that the situation across Europe varies, with Portugal in a stronger fiscal position and with much less debt than France.
"Those countries [those with higher public debt] have much less fiscal margin to act, but the main issue is that we need to resolve the problem of productivity and competitiveness at the European level," he said.
"The European economy is not growing as much as the U.S., and without economic growth, it's impossible to have better salaries and to have the resources for better public services and social support," Sarmento added.
In the second quarter of 2026, Portugal recorded the EU's highest annual increase in house prices, up 16.5% from a year earlier, according to Eurostat .
The Portuguese government is looking to increase the supply of housing to reduce buying and renting costs to resolve the issue, according to Sarmento.
French government bond yields rose and the euro weakened on Monday as the unrest added to investor concerns over France's debt and budget.
"It will be difficult to see the budget deficit come down without painful measures," Sharon Bell, senior European equity strategist at Goldman Sachs, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Monday.
"Taxes could well go up for French businesses. I think taxes may generally go up in France. Fiscal consolidation means you need to either spend less or tax more. Those things are very tricky."
Mike Bell, head of market strategy at RBC BlueBay Asset Management, said France faced a "very real risk" of a sovereign debt crisis.
"What's needed in France is to get the fiscal position in order; they need to raise the retirement age — you can't retire at 62 if the average person's living to 84 — but if this is going on even before they start talking about that, then imagine what would happen on the streets of France if you tried to raise the retirement age... I mean, here in the U.K. it's 68," Bell added.

The console industry continues to reel from the RAMpocalypse, and Xbox is certainly feeling it.
Circana analysis suggested a few weeks ago that Xbox hardware sales are at their lowest level ever , with PlayStation also suffering their lowest hardware sell-through situation since 2013. Without a doubt, the so-called RAMpocalypse is to blame, with companies like Google, Anthropic, OpenAI , and indeed, Microsoft itself buying up all the RAM for their AI -tinted ambitions.
That leaves little left over for "niche" consumer electronics scenarios, such as video game consoles ... ballooning Xbox, PlayStation, and Nintendo console prices to their highest levels ever in some cases.
The timing couldn't be worse really. Grand Theft Auto 6 launches in a month from now, and its mainstream appeal would've driven huge amounts of users to upgrade older consoles or perhaps enter the hobby for the first time. With global stock levels battered and prices otherwise impossible for most to consider, Microsoft is turning towards a novel approach to try to increase stock availability.
Spotted by users on X (cheers H!) and covered first by PowerUP , Microsoft is actually sending out emails to users who have dormant Xbox Series X |S hardware, recommending that they trade them in, offering links and advice on how to do so. The email specifically cites Best Buy, which has a trade-in system here you can explore for Xbox hardware .
It seems the emails are going out specifically to users who have hardware that they aren't actively using, including users who own multiple consoles potentially.
Indeed, the economics on console hardware is so bad right now that any user sitting on a dormant PS5 , Xbox Series X|S, or Nintendo Switch potentially represents a big net loss for the big three. The margins are so bad, and the stock availability so low, that trying to convince users to move their consoles to others who might actually become more active players (and spenders) is more than preferable.
Ahead of Grand Theft Auto 6's launch , Microsoft and its competitors are working around the clock to source components for their hardware provisions. Call of Duty has also stopped shipping on past-gen consoles, and it seems fairly likely given how popular Modern Warfare 4 has been so far that many users would want to upgrade for that as well ... if indeed there was stock available.
Stock availability of new (and very pricy) Xbox Series X|S hardware has generally remains stable in Microsoft core markets like the U.S., UK, Canada, Australia, and so on. In Asia, mainland Europe, the Middle East, and South America Xbox console stock has been almost non-existent. Tariffs, the RAMpocalypse, and general global economic instability has left the console market in a precarious state ... despite an unprecedented density of high-quality games.
Some analysts expect the "RAMpocalypse" to last through to 2028, maybe even 2029, with consumer electronics expected to take a battering between now and then. Smartphone, PC, laptop, and of course, game console shipments are all down as a direct result of the AI build out. It doesn't look like things will change any time soon.

Jez is known for breaking exclusive news and analysis as relates to the Microsoft ecosystem — while being powered by tea. articles.title_orig: Salesforce to Buy Marketing Platform Braze for $5.7 Billion
articles.title_zh: Salesforce to Buy Marketing Platform Braze for $5.7 Billion
articles.content_orig:
Shares of Salesforce slipped roughly 1% on Tuesday morning, after the company announced an agreement to buy customer engagement platform Braze for about $5.66 billion.
Under the deal, holders of Braze Class A common stock will get $47.50 in cash per share. The transaction is expected to close in fiscal 2028, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals, according to a Salesforce blog .
Braze shares closed at $30.04 on Monday. The stock skyrocketed more than 50% on Tuesday after a brief halt premarket following the news. The company makes artificial intelligence marketing tools to manage customer data and messaging.
"Salesforce shares our commitment to marketers, and we'll continue building as Braze and investing in the Braze community of customers and partners who built this company with us," Bill Magnuson, CEO of Braze, said in a statement. "Salesforce's platform will help us innovate faster and together we'll help marketers around the world build deeper, more lasting relationships with their customers."
The latest deal comes just months after Salesforce announced it would buy AI customer service platform Fin for about $3.6 billion, in a move meant to bolster the company's agentic AI offerings for enterprises.
In August, Salesforce and Anthropic announced an expanded partnership , including a new plugin called "Claudeforce" with pre-built sales skills for salespeople to better compose emails, update records and more with the frontier lab's model.
